title: Computer Networking — Packets to Campus Edge
kinesthetic_hook: Parse a crafted frame, run LPM, and prove a four-router town on paper then in code.
lesson_excerpt: The WAIKE Packet Range is a synthetic teaching fixture with four endpoints named Pier, Yard, Shed, and Roof, not evidence of a deployed campus. TCP divides its byte stream into segments; that is different
worked_example: Assume IPv4 without options (20-byte header), TCP without options (20-byte header), a 1500-byte path MTU, and no IP fragmentation. TCP payload capacity is 1500 - 20 - 20 = 1460 bytes. Sending 2000 TCP stream bytes requires at least ceil(2000/1460) = 2 data segments, for example 1460 + 540. Actual segment count can be higher. TLS adds its own bytes before TCP. On receive, peel Ethernet (ethertype 0x0800), then IPv4, then TCP. Independent practice: repeat for MTU 1280 with a 40-byte IPv6 header and 20-byte TCP header; state why your result does not count acknowledgments or retransmissions.
assignment: Draw the sticky-note stack for a TLS web fetch from Pier to a library cache. Label who reads each header. No vendor GUI screenshots required.

lesson.title: Packets are chopped on purpose
lesson.body_md:
The WAIKE Packet Range is a synthetic teaching fixture with four endpoints named Pier, Yard, Shed, and Roof, not evidence of a deployed campus. In this fixture, the path MTU is 1500 bytes: one IP packet can occupy at most 1500 bytes, including its IP header. The Ethernet header is outside that limit. Other links can have different MTUs. TCP divides its byte stream into segments; that is different from IP fragmentation.

For an HTTPS example using TCP, the nesting is HTTP data inside TLS records inside TCP segments inside IP packets inside Ethernet frames. HTTP/3 uses QUIC over UDP, so this example is not the only web stack. Each header is a sticky note for a different worker. The sticky note you peel first on receive is the one you added last on send. Learners who skip that sentence try to debug TCP checksums when the Ethernet destination MAC is wrong.

Multiplexing is why port 443 and port 22 can share one IP. The 5-tuple (src IP, dst IP, protocol, src port, dst port) distinguishes transport flows at a given observation point. NAT can rewrite the tuple. If you only look at IPs you will swear two students are 'the same traffic.'

CS144's public weekly shape (principles → transport → switching → congestion → routing) is a structure we acknowledge. We do not copy Stanford code. This week's lab starts an original Ethernet/IPv4 parse you will finish in the datapath lab.

Technical source: RFC 9293 sections 3.7 and 3.7.1, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9293.html#section-3.7. Before running code, predict the payload capacity, calculate it, then explain the assumptions. A large application write alone does not tell you an exact packet count.

## Concept and scope

A path MTU limits IP packet size on the path being modeled. TCP segmentation and IP fragmentation are different mechanisms. Header options, encapsulation and retransmission affect actual traffic; an application write does not specify an exact packet count.

## Guided practice

Run the downloadable packet model. Calculate 2000 stream bytes with MTU 1500, IPv4 header 20 and TCP header 20: 1460 bytes remain per data segment, so the minimum is two. Expected result: the arithmetic test passes. Repeat with MTU 1280, IPv6 header 40 and TCP header 20, and explain which assumptions changed. This function performs arithmetic; it does not send or capture packets.

## Independent evidence

Write an encapsulation diagram including TLS for a TCP-based HTTPS example. Label byte counts separately from protocol names. Explain why HTTP/3 would need a different transport diagram.
lesson.worked_example: Assume IPv4 without options (20-byte header), TCP without options (20-byte header), a 1500-byte path MTU, and no IP fragmentation. TCP payload capacity is 1500 - 20 - 20 = 1460 bytes. Sending 2000 TCP stream bytes requires at least ceil(2000/1460) = 2 data segments, for example 1460 + 540. Actual segment count can be higher. TLS adds its own bytes before TCP. On receive, peel Ethernet (ethertype 0x0800), then IPv4, then TCP. Independent practice: repeat for MTU 1280 with a 40-byte IPv6 header and 20-byte TCP header; state why your result does not count acknowledgments or retransmissions.

weeks.title: CIDR as a land survey, not a guessing game

lesson.title: CIDR as a land survey, not a guessing game
lesson.body_md:
10.20.30.40/26 is not 'a class C with a funny number.' /26 means 26 bits of network, 6 bits of host, 64 addresses, network 10.20.30.0, broadcast 10.20.30.63, 62 usable if you still believe in network and broadcast addresses. The host .40 lives in that block the way a house lives on a surveyed lot.

A second block 10.20.30.80/28 is 16 addresses, .80–.95, 14 usable. If you put a printer at .96 you are in the next lot and the ACL you wrote for /28 will not save you.

Longest prefix match is how a router chooses among overlapping lots. /32 beats /24 beats /16 beats /0. This is the same idea you will wire into the datapath lab, and it is why 'add a more specific' is a real change, not a superstition.

IPv6 appears as a parallel survey (128 bits, no broadcast). We do not pretend a 10-week course makes you an IPv6 designer. You will be able to say why fe80:: is link-local and why it is not a public plan.

## Concept and scope

An IPv4 prefix identifies a block by its leading bits. A /26 contains 64 addresses; under the ordinary multi-access subnet convention, the first identifies the network and the last is broadcast. /31 point-to-point links and /32 host routes need separate interpretation.

## Guided practice

Predict the block containing 192.0.2.70/26. Its network is 192.0.2.64 and broadcast is 192.0.2.127, with 62 ordinary host addresses. Run the model test to compare. Expected result: all three values match. If one differs, check whether you rounded to a 64-address boundary before subtracting reserved addresses.

## Independent evidence

Solve a different /28 using a documentation address. Show the block size, boundary, broadcast and convention for usable addresses. Add /31 and /32 tests to the worked example; document where the canonical lab's contract differs.

weeks.title: The MAC closet — learning, flooding, and VLAN 20

lesson.title: The MAC closet — learning, flooding, and VLAN 20
lesson.body_md:
Pier hangs off Gi1/0/8 on VLAN 20. Yard hangs off Gi1/0/9 on VLAN 30. A frame destined to aa:aa:aa:aa:aa:10 in VLAN 20 egresses Gi1/0/8. The same MAC in VLAN 30 is a different key. If your mental model is 'MAC table is just MAC,' you have built a VLAN leak.

Unknown unicasts flood inside the VLAN, not across it. That sentence is the difference between a campus and a party line. Trunks carry VLAN tags; access ports do not surprise patrons with tagged frames.

CCNA v1.1 Network Access is the alignment label: VLANs, trunks, STP later. We configure none of that on a real Cisco in this packet. We compute forwarding on a fixture so the idea is testable offline.

A loop without STP is how the Packet Range went dark in a previous cohort: two cables into the same closet, broadcast joy, CPU 100% on the cheap switch. Week 6 returns to that scar.

## Concept and scope

A learning Ethernet switch associates source MAC addresses with ports within a forwarding domain. Unknown destination behavior and broadcast forwarding are bounded by the VLAN. A MAC address observed in one VLAN does not automatically authorize forwarding in another.

## Guided practice

Draw a fictional table with MAC A on port 1 in VLAN 20 and MAC B on port 2 in VLAN 30. Predict forwarding for a frame to A arriving in VLAN 20, then the same destination arriving in VLAN 30. Expected interpretation: the second lookup must use VLAN 30, not reuse VLAN 20's entry. Explain the unknown-destination policy of your model rather than assuming all switches use an identical configuration.

## Independent evidence

Add a third port in VLAN 20 and trace source learning followed by a destination lookup. Record the input table and output decision. Do not change a campus switch to test this exercise.
lesson.worked_example: mac_table[(aa:aa:aa:aa:aa:10, 20)] = Gi1/0/8. Lookup with VLAN 30 misses. Isolation holds.

weeks.title: Forwarding plane — TTL, LPM, and a crafted IPv4 frame

lesson.title: Forwarding plane — TTL, LPM, and a crafted IPv4 frame
lesson.body_md:
This is the deep data-path week. You are handed a classroom-crafted Ethernet+IPv4+TCP frame. Destination MAC aa:aa:aa:aa:aa:01, ethertype 0x0800, IPv4 IHL 5, TTL 4, proto 6, src 10.20.30.14, dst 10.20.40.9. You parse bytes. You do not open Wireshark on a cafe network and call it a lab.

The forwarding table has 10.20.40.0/24 via 10.20.30.1 on eth1, a /16 on eth0, and a default out wan0. LPM must choose eth1. Adding 10.20.40.9/32 must steal the route to host9. TTL decrements; TTL 1 would drop instead of forward. That drop is a feature: loops die.

RFC 791 is the field dictionary (version, IHL, TTL, protocol, addresses). We cite it; we do not paste pages of it. Checksums are mentioned; this lab does not require you to recompute the IP checksum unless you take the stretch goal.

If you treat the frame as a string of hex without slicing 0:6, 6:12, 12:14, you will invent an ethertype from the IP version nibble and then write a sad forum post.

## Concept and scope

Forwarding selects a next hop or output using the destination and forwarding table. Longest-prefix match chooses the most specific matching prefix. An IPv4 router also decrements TTL; expiry is a separate condition from finding a route.

## Guided practice

Run the model with a default route to uplink and 192.0.2.64/26 to desk. For destination 192.0.2.70 and TTL 8, predict desk and TTL 7. Expected result: the longest-prefix test passes. Repeat with TTL 1: the model drops instead. It reports a reason but does not construct an ICMP packet or update an IP checksum.

## Independent evidence

Add a /32 route for the destination and verify precedence. Then remove all matching routes and verify the no-route result. Explain why these calculations alone do not validate the canonical byte-parsing datapath lab.
lesson.worked_example: dst 10.20.40.9 matches /24 better than /16. nh 10.20.30.1 iface eth1. TTL 4→3. Host route /32 wins when present.

weeks.title: Reliability on an unreliable wire — sequences, ACKs, AIMD on paper

lesson.title: Reliability on an unreliable wire — sequences, ACKs, AIMD on paper
lesson.body_md:
TCP (current spec RFC 9293) pretends the wire is reliable by numbering bytes and refusing to live on hope. Sequence 1000, payload 200 bytes, ACK 1200 means 'I have everything before 1200.' If ACK 1000 returns, none of that payload is safe yet.

The three-way handshake is not a personality test. SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK. Data before the handshake completes is a bug in your mental model (or an experimental Fast Open you will not implement here).

Congestion control in this course is AIMD arithmetic: cwnd 10, loss, halve to 5, then +1 per RTT. You will compute a table for 8 RTTs. You will not port a C++ TCP stack. That is the CS144 shape we refuse to copy and the WAIKE shape we can actually grade offline.

Flow control (rwnd) is the receiver's remaining belly. Congestion control is the network's remaining belly. Mixing those two words is how people tune the wrong knob.

## Concept and scope

TCP provides an ordered byte stream to applications using mechanisms including sequence numbers, acknowledgments and retransmission. Acknowledgment of bytes is not a guarantee that an application saved them durably. Congestion control addresses network load; receive-window flow control addresses receiver capacity.

## Guided practice

On paper, label three non-overlapping data ranges: bytes 0–99, 100–199 and 200–299 in a simplified relative sequence space. Suppose only the first and third arrive. Expected result: a cumulative acknowledgment cannot claim the missing contiguous range has arrived. Explain why selective acknowledgment, when used, can communicate additional receipt information without making the stream gap disappear.

## Independent evidence

Trace a retransmission and distinguish duplicate arrival from duplicate application delivery. State that your diagram omits connection setup, sequence-number wrap and timers. Do not infer real throughput or congestion behavior from this paper trace.
lesson.worked_example: seq=1000 len=200 → ACK 1200 on full receipt. cwnd 10, loss → 5, then 6,7,8... on additive increase per RTT without further loss.

weeks.title: When VLANs meet a loop — STP as a circuit breaker

lesson.title: When VLANs meet a loop — STP as a circuit breaker
lesson.body_md:
Rapid PVST+ is a CCNA v1.1 phrase. In the Packet Range we treat STP as a circuit breaker: one forwarding tree per VLAN, blocked ports that would otherwise loop. Root bridge is the switch with the best priority+MAC, not the one closest to the coffee.

BPDU guard on access ports is how a volunteer plugging a 'helpful' mini-switch does not become the new root. You will explain that sentence in plain English. You will not paste Cisco config from a dump.

EtherChannel is two cables acting as one logical link so a single unplug does not partition Yard. It is not 'more Internet.' Misconfigured channel (one side on, one side off) is a loop factory.

Week 3's scar returns as a postmortem: which port should have been blocking, which VLAN flooded, and what evidence (CPU, MAC flapping) you would collect next time.

## Concept and scope

A Layer-2 forwarding loop can circulate frames and amplify broadcasts. A spanning-tree protocol chooses a loop-free active topology while retaining alternative physical links according to its rules. A blocked forwarding port is not necessarily a broken cable.

## Guided practice

Draw three fictional switches linked in a triangle. Mark one logical edge non-forwarding for your simplified model. Trace a broadcast over the active edges and count the copies per edge. Expected result: the active graph has no cycle. Remove one active link and draw a proposed replacement tree, labeling the reconfiguration as simulated.

## Independent evidence

Explain what measurements would be needed to evaluate a real protocol's convergence and disruption. Never connect an unauthorized loop to a real network. A diagram proves only a property of the graph you drew.
lesson.worked_example: Two access cables into one closet without STP → storm. BPDU guard on access would err-disable the volunteer mini-switch instead of electing it root.

weeks.title: Four-router town — SPF beats the scenic route

lesson.title: Four-router town — SPF beats the scenic route
lesson.body_md:
Routers A (Pier), B (Yard), C (Shed), D (Roof). Costs: A-B 2, B-D 2, A-C 5, C-D 5, B-C 9. Shortest A→D is A-B-D cost 4, not A-C-D cost 10. SPF is just Dijkstra on a weighted graph. OSPFv2 (RFC 2328) is the protocol that floods the graph; this lab computes the graph you already know.

A routing table is not a suggestion. If Roof's LAN is 10.20.40.0/24, Pier installs that prefix via Yard. Administrative distance is a CCNA word for 'who do I trust when two protocols argue.' Static vs OSPF is enough for this course.

First-hop redundancy is postponed to a paragraph: two gateways, one VIP, so a brick dying does not isolate the kiosk VLAN. We do not implement VRRP here.

You will trace one packet from Pier to Roof using last week's datapath plus this week's route. That is IP connectivity as a story, not a memorized command list.

## Concept and scope

A routing algorithm computes paths from a model of topology and costs. Dijkstra's algorithm assumes nonnegative edge weights. A shortest modeled path need not be the fastest measured path if configured costs do not represent measured latency.

## Guided practice

Use edges A–B cost 2, B–D cost 2, A–C cost 5 and C–D cost 5. Compare A–B–D cost 4 with A–C–D cost 10. Expected result: the first is cheaper under these configured costs. Remove B–D and recompute rather than continuing to report the old answer.

## Independent evidence

Add another route with an equal total cost. Document how your chosen model resolves ties. Explain why this calculation does not demonstrate OSPF packet exchange, a vendor implementation or real failover time.
lesson.worked_example: dijkstra(A)['D']=4 via B. Scenic A-C-D=10 loses. Install 10.20.40.0/24 nh=Yard.

weeks.title: DHCP, DNS, NAT — services that lie for us on purpose

lesson.title: DHCP, DNS, NAT — services that lie for us on purpose
lesson.body_md:
DHCP hands out leases so Pier does not keep a paper IP ledger. DNS walks stub → TLD → authoritative, then caches. The lab's second lookup must hit cache. NAT maps 10.20.30.14 to 192.0.2.88 so the library cache on the far side can answer without knowing our inside lot.

Lying is the feature: NAT lies about addresses, DNS lies about 'this name is that number for now,' DHCP lies about 'you may use this for 3600 seconds.' Troubleshooting is asking which liar expired.

NTP, syslog, SNMP appear as a CCNA IP Services chorus. In WAIKE you will timestamp lab JSON and write one syslog line. You will not stand up a full NMS.

A cache that never expires is how a moved printer becomes a ghost. TTL 300 on an A record is a policy. Set it, write it, do not blame 'the Internet.' When Roof moves to a new address at 16:00 and Pier still prints to the old one at 16:10, the liar is the cache, not the cable.

## Concept and scope

DHCP supplies configured network parameters; DNS maps names and record types; NAT translates selected address or port information. These functions are related operationally but a success in one is not proof that the others or the application work.

## Guided practice

Build a fictional diagnosis table with columns address configuration, name result, connection result and application response. Include one case where lookup succeeds but the connection fails. Expected interpretation: replacing DNS configuration is not yet justified. Include another case where a private name is absent from a public resolver; identify the intended authorized resolver before taking action.

## Independent evidence

Write a five-step troubleshooting procedure that tests one layer at a time. Record which outcomes are simulated. Avoid sending private hostnames or real packet captures to public tools for this exercise.
lesson.worked_example: First resolve desk.gary.waike.example → 203.0.113.14 via auth_walk. Second → cache. NAT inside 10.20.30.14 outside 192.0.2.88.

weeks.title: ACLs that actually order, and the telnet we refuse

lesson.title: ACLs that actually order, and the telnet we refuse
lesson.body_md:
An ACL is a story told top to bottom. Deny tcp/23, permit tcp/443, deny *. Telnet is a classroom fossil we refuse at the edge. HTTPS to the library cache is allowed. Port 9 discard is denied by the star rule — implicit deny made visible.

DHCP snooping and ARP inspection are named so you can recognize a CCNA Security Fundamentals neighbor. We implement neither on silicon. We do write why a rogue DHCP under the table hands out 192.168.1.1 as a gateway and steals a cohort afternoon.

WPA3 is a wireless security word you should be able to place next to 'guest SSID is isolated.' This is not a wireless engineering course (that is WIRELESS_6G, still alive as an advanced track).

SSH not telnet, HTTPS not HTTP for staff tools, and no 'permit ip any any' at the top because that line is how ACLs become wallpaper.

## Concept and scope

An ordered access-control list applies its configured match and decision policy. A broad early permit can make a later deny unreachable. NAT translation is not a substitute for an explicit authorization policy.

## Guided practice

Model first-match rules: deny destination port 23; permit port 443; deny everything else. Trace ports 23, 443 and 9. Expected results: deny, permit, deny. Swap the final deny to the first position and predict that all three requests are denied. Treat ports as fixture fields, not proof of the application running on them.

## Independent evidence

Add source-prefix conditions and test a case just outside the allowed prefix. Show the ordered rules and matching rule index. Do not apply this experimental policy to a live firewall. Include an approved rollback plan for any future operational exercise.
lesson.worked_example: decide(23)=deny, decide(443)=permit, decide(9)=deny. NAT still maps the inside host.

weeks.title: Campus edge capstone — intent files and a datapath proof

lesson.title: Campus edge capstone — intent files and a datapath proof
lesson.body_md:
You will ship a JSON intent file: VLANs, prefixes, ACL order, NAT, and the four-router costs. A tiny validator will reject missing next-hops. That is the automation domain without pretending we built a controller fabric.

The practical exam is the datapath lab plus a written trace of one packet from Pier to Roof including VLAN, LPM, TTL, and ACL. If those four nouns are not in the trace, the practical is incomplete.

Group project: redesign the Packet Range for a public Saturday with a guest VLAN that cannot reach Roof management. Present for eight minutes. No slide template from the old campus UPNOW generator — your topology is specific.

Career: this course aligns to CCNA v1.1 domains and to CS144's build-the-path ethos. It does not grant CCNA. It does not include Stanford solutions. If a recruiter asks 'did you pass CCNA,' the honest answer is 'I can show a datapath trace and an intent file,' not 'yes.' That sentence belongs in the portfolio.

## Concept and scope

An integrated network claim needs linked evidence: intent, inputs, implementation, observations and limits. A route calculation, parsed fixture and connectivity observation support different claims. A successful ping does not establish that a TLS service is authorized or correct.

## Guided practice

Assemble prefix calculations, encapsulation diagram, forwarding cases, ACL traces and a diagnosis record. Run the seven downloadable model tests, preserve the output, then deliberately reverse longest-prefix selection and observe the test failure. Restore and rerun. Expected result: your evidence identifies the controlled defect and the corrected version.

## Independent evidence

Submit a claim-to-test table with one unsupported claim explicitly rejected. Keep physical-network observations separate from local calculations. Completion requires the canonical practical artifacts and authorized review; page visits and this worked example are insufficient.
lesson.worked_example: Intent JSON must include prefix 10.20.40.0/24 nh via Yard, ACL deny 23, datapath ok=true.
